title: Monitoring training in athletes with reference to overtraining syndrome
population: Experienced athletes recording session RPE x duration; observational
findings: Observations in 25 experienced athletes who recorded training by integrating session RPE with session duration.
Banal illnesses were correlated with training load (rolling 6-week average), monotony (daily mean/standard deviation) and strain (load x monotony).
A high percentage of illnesses could be accounted for when individual athletes exceeded individually identifiable training thresholds, mostly related to the strain of training.
Simple monitoring of training characteristics may let athletes achieve training goals while minimizing undesired outcomes.
limitations: Small sample (n=25), mixed athletes, observational and correlational with illness as the outcome; thresholds were individual, not universal; no numeric thresholds in the abstract; abstract does not state whether the design was prospective. Strain/monotony have since been questioned in the wider literature (not assessed here).
implications: Compute weekly load (session RPE x minutes or HR-based proxy), monotony and strain; show them descriptively and flag only when an athlete's own value exceeds their personal historical range.
Keep daily load varied (hard-easy days) to limit monotony; supports scheduled recovery weeks.

verification.notes: Crossref and PubMed match (MSSE 1998;30(7):1164-8). Design changed from 'prospective-cohort' to 'other' because the abstract only says 'observations'.
